fn.en: Choose the right present tense: what you usually do, and what is different today.

items.q: Three words that mean “now, while we are speaking”: at the ___.
The word that means “nearly always, as a rule”.
Two words for “in this period of life, not before”: these ___.
A verb you almost never use with -ing: to ___ the answer.
Another verb you almost never use with -ing: to ___ a coffee.
And one more: to ___ help.

lines: I usually [take|am taking|takes] the bus, but today I [’m walking|walk|walks]. 🚌
She normally [wears|is wearing|wear] a suit, but this week she [’s wearing|wears|wear] jeans. 👖
We [live|are living|lives] in Almaty, but at the moment we [’re staying|stay|stays] with my sister. 🏨
He [works|is working|work] in a bank, but these days he [’s working|works|work] from home. 💻
I [know|am knowing|knows] the answer, and I [want|am wanting|wants] to say it. 🧠

sub.en: Look at the pairs. Which time words go with each tense — and which verbs never take -ing?

items.q: I ___ to work every day.
items.why: every day / usually / normally → Present Simple.

items.q: Today I ___ because my car is at the garage.
items.why: today / at the moment / right now → Present Continuous.

items.q: She ___ in a bank, but this week she’s at a conference.
Look — it ___! Take your umbrella.
It ___ a lot here in November.
I ___ the answer.
items.why: know, like, want, need and have (= own) describe a state, not an action. They stay in the simple.

items.q: She ___ two brothers.
“What ___ you doing?” — “I’m cooking.”

items.a: At the moment they’re staying with friends
These days he’s working from home

items.from: It rains a lot in November.

tts: Anita and Paul are having a meeting with their boss.

items.x: Paul wears a suit to work.
They work in the same office.

tts: Where are you? — I’m in a clothes shop.
What are you doing? — What do people usually do in clothes shops? I’m buying clothes, of course.
I’m trying to cook a meal for six people, and the kids are making a lot of noise and the dog’s running around.
Why are the kids there? They go to tennis practice on Thursdays. — Not today, because it’s raining.

items.q: “I’m buying clothes” is about
“What do people usually do in clothes shops?” is about
“The dog’s running around” is about
“They go to tennis practice on Thursdays” is about
“It’s raining” is about
The two tenses in this call are

items.sit: You normally take the bus. Today your car is at the garage and you are on foot.
o: I usually take the bus, but today I’m walking.
I usually am taking the bus, but today I walk.
I usually take the bus, but today I walk.

items.sit: Your colleague normally wears a suit. This week she is in jeans.
o: She normally wears a suit, but this week she’s wearing jeans.
She is normally wearing a suit, but this week she wears jeans.
She normally wear a suit, but this week she wearing jeans.

items.sit: Someone asks if you understand. You do.
o: Yes, I am knowing the answer.

items.sit: You look out of the window. Water is falling right now.
Your friend asks about your job. You are at home more than before.
o: These days I’m working from home.
These days I working from home.
These days I am work from home.

items.sit: Someone asks how many brothers you have. You have two.

lines.s: Nothing much. I ___ with my sister this week. 🏨
In the centre. But they’re painting my flat.
Are you going out this evening?
Do you want to come to us instead?
I don’t ___ yet. I’ll call you at six. 🧠

write.q: Write 6 sentences with both tenses. Three about what you usually do, and three about what is different today or this week. Use one state verb (know, like, want, need, have).
write.model: I usually get up at seven, but this week I’m getting up at six, because we start early. I normally take the bus, but today I’m walking. I work in an office, but these days I’m working from home two days a week. I like my job. I don’t need a car at the moment. I know it will change in September.

speak.q: Say three pairs out loud: “I usually…, but today I’m…”. Then answer: What are you doing right now? What do you do every day?
speak.model: I usually drink tea, but today I’m drinking coffee. I usually walk, but this week I’m taking the bus. Right now I’m studying English. Every day I check my emails at nine.
